column47: The MS program in biomedical engineering (BME) is intended for students with an undergraduate degree in an engineering discipline or a physical or biological science who wish to pursue a career in the field of biomedical engineering in industry, government, or academia. Students in the program will be educated in the core fundamentals of biomedical engineering through didactic coursework and a mentored research or design project. Coursework can be selected from one of four specializations: biomaterials, biomechanics, biomedical data science, or medical physics. The mentored research/design requirement can be completed by a thesis, a project, or a portfolio option. For the thesis and project options, the student works with a faculty mentor on a research/design project that culminates in a written thesis or project report and a public presentation. For the portfolio option, the student works with a faculty mentor on a series of at least three smaller research/design projects that culminate in a portfolio summarizing the projects. Students can also elect a coursework-only option in medical physics that requires the completion of 30 credits of coursework from the medical physics specialization. This option is intended for students with significant prior research or design experience.

[2] The program includes a combination of 36 credits in media theory, media culture, media production, and computer science, with electives in bioinformatics/biostatistics, biology, computer science, geography, mathematics, and electrical engineering. [5] Students select electives commensurate with their interests, background, and experience. [5] Graduates will be well suited for positions in design, usability, and user-facing engineering as well as the increasingly prevalent number of computational- and media-focused PhD programs emphasizing a combination of theoretical and practical application. [2] Students ultimately embark on writing an MS Thesis or a producing a research project (or some combination thereof) under faculty guidance in areas such as Gaming; Mobile, Social and Computational Media; Virtual Reality; Bio Art; and Interaction Design. [5]
